guard: cotal_send still creates unknown channels, but the success receipt lets a caller tell a new name from a known one
why: Issue #989. A typo'd channel used to return the same success line as a send into a known
room. The discriminating assertion is that a caller can TELL, not that bogus send fails.
N1 restores the old identical success TEMPLATE (drop the receipt). The cell that
normalized success lines differ must redden. Raw strings still differ by channel name.
N2 makes closeChannelNames always empty, so a one-edit typo no longer names the match.
N3 makes every name look pre-existing, so the tool receipt never says new channel.
N5 makes the authed default the first concrete channel again: the live Cloud refusal on #announce.
N6 drops the refusal when no read channel is postable.
N7 sends the raw argument instead of the resolved default.
N8 drops the explicit channel check, so a pattern or a malformed name is described and handed to send.
N9 drops the connected-followers way from the refusal for a pattern with *.
N10 drops both ways from the advertised channel text.
N11 gives a name that breaks the channel grammar the pattern advice.
N12 drops the no-stored-copies caveat from the refusal for a pattern with *.
N13 lets a malformed name with no whole-segment wildcard through, so team.** is sent as team.__.
N14 shows a long name whole in the refusal instead of its first 64 characters.
N15 drops the channel grammar from the no-channel-name refusal.
N16 states a limit other than core's MAX_CHANNEL_LENGTH in the no-channel-name refusal.
N17 and N18 move the cut threshold one character either way.
N19 cuts in the wrong place: the first 63 characters and then the last one.
N20 cuts in the wrong place by putting ten earlier characters where the last ten belong.
N21 echoes a name over the limit whole after the refusal.
N22 refuses a valid name of exactly the limit.
N23 drops the stored-copy way from the refusal for a family (#5404).
N24 and N25 swap the family and the pattern-with-* advice.
N26 drops the stored copy from the advertised channel text.
N27 puts the old bare line back for a known channel, so the result again says only that it was sent.
N28 drops "Agents on it see it too" from the mention line, so a mention reads like a DM.
N29 ignores the channel's replay setting in the line, and N30 stops the tool passing it, so a
channel that does not replay still promises later joiners the post.
N31 drops the DM line's guidance, so a DM again says nothing about the task's channel.
N32 drops the cotal_dm description's sentence that sends a status for a peer to the task's
channel with a mention.
N33 restores the claim that a live channel reaches every connected agent, which SPEC §4 does not
give a busy one. N34 offers once on every harness, though the manager refuses it without turn relay.
NO BUILD STEP: the suite imports ../src.
